item.title: Herdr Configuration in Depth: 208 Keys Across 14 Sections, and What "I Reloaded but Nothing Changed" Really Means
item.description: Reorganise Herdr's 208 configuration keys by which process owns them and when they take effect, rather than by name: where the config file lives and the Windows difference, how to use the 377-line herdr --default-config, the real output of herdr config check and server reload-config, what a reload applies to and what it cannot (pane defaults, worktrees, integrations, and custom commands belong to the server; themes, sidebar, and copy behaviour belong to the client), the real rules behind headless_cols and headless_rows, the trade-offs in the three terminal keys, the difference between keys.prefix and direct keys, and the observation that experimental.allow_nested is exactly the nested-launch gate from module 4. Includes a 14-section key-count table and a risk ranking of the experimental keys. Baseline herdr 0.9.2.

item.title: Herdr Keyboard Control: the Prefix Key, Five Keys to Learn First, copy mode, and a prefix-free Scheme That Does Not Fight Back
item.description: The complete breakdown of Herdr's keyboard layer: why the prefix key exists (the OS, the outer terminal and the program in the pane all claim keystrokes), the five keys worth learning first (prefix+c/v/minus/h-j-k-l/w/q), the full pane/tab/workspace binding table, the editing keys of Herdr's own text fields, copy-mode movement and search rules; the [keys] binding syntax (prefix may be an array, one action may bind several keys, named punctuation, indexed 1..9), the four [[keys.command]] types popup/pane/shell/plugin_action, and the official ctrl+alt prefix-free scheme measured across 10 terminals along with the combinations you must avoid.

item.title: Module 1: Daily Workflow (mouse-first, keyboard, session state)
item.description: Everyday Herdr use: the mouse-first workflow (clicking panes, dragging split borders, right-click menus), the ctrl+b prefix and a prefix-free keybinding scheme, and the precise differences between the five state paths: detach / snapshot restore / history replay / agent-native resume / live handoff. Baseline herdr 0.9.2 stable.
